title: Automated CRD projection mismatch resolution for private-cluster upgrades
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Summary: Multiple private/VPC customer escalations have traced recurring post-upgrade failures to a class of operator <CRD projection mismatches> where the operator's computed projected status diverges from Helm's post-upgrade rendered resources. Symptoms include nodegroup registration failures, controller restart thrash, and stuck Helm releases in a 'pending' state.

Problem statement: During rolling upgrades of the on-prem operator, concurrent controller restarts + concurrent Helm reconciliation can lead to resource representations that the operator interprets as invalid (missing required projection fields) even though Helm believes the release succeeded. These mismatches block normal reconciliation and require manual intervention (kubectl patch / helm rollback) for affected customers. Current mitigations are manual runbooks and ad-hoc hotfix PRs. We need a robust automated reconciliation path that is safe by default and auditable to reduce customer impact and mean time to recovery (MTTR).
acceptance_criteria: A safe automated reconciler is implemented that detects projection mismatches between operator-computed CRD state and Helm-rendered resources
The reconciler performs a non-destructive three-way merge (observed, desired-from-helm, last-applied) and only auto-applies changes when they are additive or explicitly modeled as safe to reconcile
Feature is gated behind a feature-flag and enabled in dry-run for all existing private clusters for 2 weeks before full enablement
A customer-facing runbook and internal post-mortem template are published and linked from the Console incident view
E2E tests and upgrade canary (5% of upgraders in staging-like infra) pass without introducing data loss or increased error rates
Metric instrumentation exists to show reconciler decisions (auto-applied, skipped, required-manual) and is visible in Console for affected customers
implementation_notes:
Design: Build a projection-reconciler component in operator that performs schema-aware three-way merge using last-applied-annotation when available. Steps: 1) On detection of mismatch, record diagnostic event and compute three inputs: observed (cluster), desired (Helm manifest rendered via helm template using current chart values), and last-applied (annotation). 2) Run an idempotency and safety checker: deny destructive deletes of fields marked immutable, require manual approval for secret/credential rotations, allow additive list/field merges. 3) When safe, apply a minimal patch (server-side apply preferred) and emit an audit entry (k8s event + operator-audit log). 4) If not safe, annotate CR with 'reconcile_blocker' and escalate to on-call via Slack webhook and incident channel.

Trade-offs: Adds operator complexity and some latency to reconciliation. We limit scope to projection-related fields and gating via feature flag to reduce blast radius. We will NOT attempt automated schema migrations (out of scope for this ticket).
rollout_plan:
1) Merge reconciler behind feature-flag to main; 2) Run dry-run across all private clusters for 14 days and collect metrics; 3) Enable auto-apply for internal QA clusters; 4) Canary enable for 5% of private upgrades with monitoring alerts; 5) Gradual ramp to 100% with weekly review. Feature-flag controls: dry-run, allowed-field-whitelist, require-manual-for-critical.

Rollback: Feature-flag toggle and operator patch to quickly disable reconciler. If reconciler caused regressions, revert to previous operator release and run targeted manual remediation PRs (documented in runbook).
test_plan:
Unit tests for three-way merge edge cases. Integration tests: simulated Helm/Operator concurrent upgrade harness that reproduces projection mismatch scenarios. E2E upgrade test: full private cluster upgrade with canary and observability. Post-deploy validation: assert no stuck Helm releases, nodegroups register within SLO window, and reconciler metrics show <1% required-manual after full rollout.

Test artifacts: upgrade simulation scripts in repo 'infra/upgrade-harness' (internal), CI job operator-reconciler-e2e (pipeline: https://github.com/redwood-inference/operator/pipelines/PR-9812).

Decision: restrict auto-apply to additive fields and lists; require manual approval for immutable/credential fields. Action: add schema whitelist. Confluence design doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/OPS/CRD+Projection+Reconciler

2026-03-03 - After synthetic tests, noticed race where last-applied annotation missing for older clusters. Added fallback heuristic to compute last-applied from Helm history. Filed follow-up ENG-100498 to backfill annotations during minor patch window.

2026-03-09 - Internal dry-run started in staging. Early metrics: 0.9% of reconciliations would have auto-applied; 0.6% required manual intervention. Created dashboard: https://console.redwood.ai/dashboards/operator/reconciler-2026-03
